solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bachelors visiting famous footballer ruin external wall-coating

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so the bachelors end up sitting within the footballer's name

blocks.note: Pelé, the Brazilian forward, is the crossword's favourite footballer
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, and there are two of them
to dash hopes is to ruin them

explanation.surface: A star footballer, hosting a stag party, damages the rendering on the outside of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebbledash is a render of cement with small stones pressed in, applied to the outside of buildings.

clue.text: Stylish being finally leaving for pub — a rogue, possibly?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word being
one letter leaves its place and something else takes it, a swap rather than a plain removal

blocks.note: stylish and elegant are synonyms
the closing letter of being
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A smart creature quits for the pub, which might mark it out as a bit of a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of ELEGANT is swapped out for PH, giving ELEPHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue elephant is a lone, aggressive animal driven from its herd, so the beast is one possible kind of rogue.

clue.text: Stole keys, pinching ring

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between two points, so the keys squeeze the ring between them

blocks.note: B and A are two musical keys
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A thief took the keys, also nicking a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like the past tense of steal, but it is the noun for a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long fluffy scarf of feathers or fur, a type of stole worn around the shoulders.

clue.text: Tree identified by European of skeletal build

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
someone of skeletal build is bony

explanation.surface: A thin European botanist names a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical hardwood tree prized for its dense black timber.

clue.text: Judge a champ right to corner leader of rebels

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of rebels
to corner something is to hem it in, so the earlier letters close around the later one

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of rebels
to champ is to bite or chew noisily
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A judge orders a champion to trap the rebel leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A, BITE and R together make ABITER, which closes around the R of rebels just after its first letter, giving ARBITER.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, so the word works as a noun for a judge.

clue.text: Obstruction old peasant originally negotiated in athletic event

indicators.note: originally points to where a word begins, its opening letter
in places one letter inside the word for the athletic event

blocks.note: a hind was a farm labourer in old Scotland and northern England
a race is an athletic event
the opening letter of negotiated

explanation.surface: An old farmhand gets past a hurdle at a sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is anything that gets in the way, so it is a synonym for an obstruction.

clue.text: Bloke with yen for evidence of 21 across?

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person or bloke
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A man longs for proof of a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is MURDER, and yen looks like a longing but is the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is the classic sign that a killing has happened, hence the question mark for this example.

clue.text: Puzzle touring Aintree bars

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the letters move about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A conundrum: a pub crawl around the bars at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainteaser is a problem set to test thinking, a synonym for a puzzle.

clue.text: Clarify MacDiarmid’s last poem about City area

indicators.note: last points to the closing letter of the poet's name
about means surrounding, so the letters wrap around the area

blocks.note: the closing letter of MacDiarmid
EC is the postcode for the City of London
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A request to explain the final poem by Hugh MacDiarmid about part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh MacDiarmid was a Scottish poet; the City is the financial district of London, and its postcodes begin with those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode is to work out the meaning of something obscure, which makes it clear.

clue.text: Underworld goddess mostly associated with old doctor’s sacrifice

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the goddess's name loses its final letter

blocks.note: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft linked with the underworld
O is the abbreviation for old
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An offering to a goddess of the dead, arranged with an old physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was a large ritual offering of cattle in ancient Greece, a great sacrifice.

clue.text: Shade sister found outside a church

indicators.note: something found outside another surrounds it, so the sister wraps around the a

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun stands in the shade outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle gradation of meaning or colour, as a shade is.

clue.text: Particular house in warm and friendly environment

indicators.note: in places the house inside the word for the cosy setting

blocks.note: a cosy place is warm and friendly
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A fussy buyer wants a home with a cosy atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular person is fussy and hard to please, which is what choosy means.

clue.text: High-handed with regard to deportment

blocks.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
bearing is the way a person carries themselves

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being imperious about posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing describes someone domineering and arrogant, the same sense as high-handed.

clue.text: Lament retired academic unknown by most of the proverbial crowd, it’s said

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the academic's title runs backwards
most of means not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the saying goes two's company, three's a crowd
a don is a university teacher
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A grumbling professor in retirement is ignored by most people.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song or poem of mourning for the dead, a formal lament.

clue.text: Bury receiver, ringing about distortion of signal

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the receiver's letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
a fence receives and sells stolen goods
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone wants a radio set buried because its reception is crackling.
explanation.walkthrough: Receiver looks like a radio, but it is the criminal fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Interference is the disruption of a broadcast by unwanted noise from other sources.

clue.text: Manhandle head of gang in from entrance, perhaps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of gang
in places that letter inside the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of gang
an archway is one kind of entrance

explanation.surface: The gang leader is roughly hauled in through the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To frogmarch is to force someone forward with arms held behind their back, a rough handling.

clue.text: Articles granny pens primarily in Greek

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the word in
to pen is to enclose, as livestock in a fold

blocks.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles
nan is a British pet name for a grandmother
the opening letter of in

explanation.surface: Grandma writes newspaper pieces mostly in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles looks like newspaper pieces, but it means the grammatical words a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian comes from Athens, so the word is one specific kind of Greek.

clue.text: Doctor visited Rio, taken in by ecological variety

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order
something taken in by another is held inside it

blocks.note: taken as written: ten letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor went to Rio de Janeiro and was impressed by the range of wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the person who visited, but it is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Biodiversity is the range of living species in an ecosystem, its variety of life.

clue.text: Reserved protégé knocked over in pub – enumeration error, this should read

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word for protégé is read backwards
in places that word inside the pub

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
a ward is someone under another's protection
surface padding: an editor's note correcting a misprinted letter count, not wordplay

explanation.surface: A shy young charge gets knocked down in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Protégé looks like the person knocked over, but it only supplies a word to turn round inside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn can describe someone withdrawn and introspective, which matches reserved.

clue.text: Marketplace stocking new fur

indicators.note: a shop stocking an item holds it inside

blocks.note: the agora was the marketplace of an ancient Greek city
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A market stall is selling a novel fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is the soft fine hair of the Angora rabbit or goat, used as a fur and fibre.

clue.text: Blue berets rushed round back of farm, suffering no hurt

indicators.note: the back of a word is its closing letter, here of farm
round means encircling, so the running word goes around that letter

blocks.note: UN peacekeepers wear blue berets
to hare is to run very fast
the closing letter of farm

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping soldiers ran around a farm and nobody was injured.
explanation.definitionFit: Unharmed means not injured or damaged, the state of having suffered no hurt.

clue.text: Dispatch old racehorse from the East

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: Red Rum won the Grand National three times in the 1970s

explanation.surface: An instruction to send away an old racehorse from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the famous British steeplechaser, and the reversal was a plot point in The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them, so the verb is a euphemism for murder.

clue.text: Chap fencing in quiet wood

indicators.note: fencing in means enclosing, so the chap surrounds the quiet sign

blocks.note: a chap is a male
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A man is putting up a fence in a peaceful forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is the timber of the maple tree, a hard wood used for furniture and flooring.

clue.text: One who manages without current reproducing device

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the manager wraps around the current

blocks.note: a coper is someone who copes or manages
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone who gets by with no electricity owns a duplicating machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier is an office machine that makes duplicates of documents.

clue.text: Download tip backing team: it may be found in a book

definitions.text: it may be found in a book

indicators.note: backing here means moving backwards, so the team's numeral is written in reverse

blocks.note: an app is a program you download
the tip of something is its end
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A betting tip downloaded to back a team, found in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip and backing suggest a racing bet, but the book is a printed volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material at the end of a book, so it is one thing found there.

clue.text: Disappointing score upset trendy musical in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top
in the end points to the closing letter of musical

blocks.note: in means fashionable
the closing letter of musical; the run of letters across musical in read backwards is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A fashionable show ends in an upsetting flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means zero, a score nobody hopes to post in a game.

clue.text: Report gladly at first on prohibition

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of gladly

blocks.note: a ban is a prohibition
the opening letter of gladly

explanation.surface: Someone reports happily on a new ban.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, G on BAN means G follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud explosive noise, as from a gun, which is a bang.

clue.text: Thinner lad working in undeveloped area

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A skinny boy has a job out in the back of beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinterland is the remote, thinly settled region behind a coast or city, lacking development.
